transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-08
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Wong (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Orion Head of ML), Connor Blake (Orion Platform), Priya Nair (Orion PM)

Summary (auto): quick sync on model perf, agree which variant to pin for pilot, action items to run throughput tests and hand off security docs

00:00 Samir Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining quick check in today, agenda is short, results review and decide what to pin for next week
00:22 Maya Ortiz: great, yeah we got the eval spreadsheet, thanks, we ran the conversational rerank and the summarization prompt sets against the candidate models
00:35 Connor Blake: quick note, traffic is still synthetic from our staging but we did spike tests to 300 rps, so keep that in mind
00:50 Leah Wong: cool, so the high level from our side, model A-v2 (float16) has best quality on our NLU tests but costs ~1.8x tokens vs model B-quant, B-quant is cheaper but hallucination rate was slightly higher on long context
01:10 Priya Nair: when you say hallucination higher, is that on the 2k window or longer? our use case often exceeds 4k in product flows
01:25 Leah Wong: mostly 4k+, we saw more drift after 3k tokens, A-v2 held up better past 5k, whereas B-quant struggled with entity consistency, could be quantization artifacts or KV-cache truncation
01:45 Maya Ortiz: ok that's useful, cost matters but quality is our top metric for pilot acceptance, we need precision on order extraction and dates
02:01 Samir Patel: understood; proposal: pin A-v2 for core checkout flow where correctness is mandatory, and configure fallback to B-quant for lower-priority routes, also enable prefix caching to reduce cost on repeated contexts
02:22 Connor Blake: how hard is rolling back if we see perf regressions? our infra team wants to avoid manual steps during business hours
02:35 Leah Wong: rollbacks are automated in Redwood via rollout policies - we can do a canary 10% to 50% with auto-fallback on error thresholds and increased latency. If error rate > 2% or latency > 400ms P50 we auto revert to previous pinned variant
02:58 Connor Blake: that auto revert sounds good, will we get traces/alerts integrated into our pager?
03:10 Samir Patel: yes we can push tracing hooks and webhooks to your SRE channel, also send token-level cost breakdowns per route
03:22 Priya Nair: about the cost numbers, the sheet shows A-v2 at 1.8x cost but with higher latency in peak, B-quant lower cost but slightly lower throughput under batching? was that right
03:39 Leah Wong: yes B-quant saturates earlier because quant kernels on that hardware had lower peak throughput in our tests, but it's cheaper per token. Also we can try mixed strategy: A-v2 for critical endpoints, B-quant as overflow via routing policy by latency/cost tier
03:58 Maya Ortiz: curious about private deployment options - any blockers for us to try private for pilot? we have data residency needs for EU clients
04:12 Samir Patel: for pilot we usually start hosted to iterate fast, but we can provision a private VPC deployment if needed. Private has extra setup: network peering, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and SOC2 addendum if required
04:33 Connor Blake: SSO and audit logs are must-haves, will you provide SAML and audit log streams? We need to show this to security
04:45 Leah Wong: yes SAML SSO and audit logs are supported, also you can opt in to extended retention for logs as an add-on. We'll attach the security deck and SOC2 report after the call
05:03 Priya Nair: any known incompatibilities with our on-prem vector DB? we use an older version of the embedding store
05:18 Samir Patel: usually fine; embedding outputs are just payloads, but we can validate end-to-end, Connor if you can share a small sample we'll run an integration check
05:32 Connor Blake: I'll get that to you, plus the exact traffic schedule so benching matches production patterns
05:44 Maya Ortiz: back to model pinning - we need at least two stable variants, one primary and one fallback. Does Redwood support weighted rollouts if we want to test alternate prompt tuning?
06:00 Leah Wong: yes weighted routing by percentage and route policies by model tag, you can test prompt-tuned variants as separate model versions and route 5-10% through them, maintain metrics comparison
06:20 Samir Patel: quick note on metrics: we'll show per-route quality evals and token-cost per 1k requests so you can decide the break-even points
06:33 Maya Ortiz: timeline wise we want to freeze pinned models before the pilot starts on 2027-06-15 so we have a week for burn-in
06:45 Samir Patel: sounds good, propose to pin A-v2 for checkout and B-quant as fallback for search/summary, run dedicated throughput test this week and get rollback thresholds set
06:58 Leah Wong: I'll run the benchmark on a p4d equivalent, 1k, 3k and 5k token profiles, capture latency percentiles and GPU utilization, upload logs to the shared folder
07:15 Connor Blake: for the bench, please also include KV cache warm/cold runs, we saw big diff when cache was cold during morning ramps
07:29 Leah Wong: good point, we'll include warm/cold runs and also test prefix caching scenarios
07:42 Priya Nair: any pricing change if we pin a higher-cost model for only a subset of routes? we want to avoid unexpected overages
07:54 Samir Patel: we can model expected spend in the spreadsheet, and set budget caps per route; Redwood will alert when spend hits thresholds and can auto-route to cheaper variants if desired
08:12 Maya Ortiz: ok let's capture the ACCEPTANCE criteria: 1) checkout extraction accuracy >= 97% on our test set, 2) P95 latency < 800ms on peak, 3) cost stays within forecast +/- 10%
08:33 Samir Patel: noted, we'll add that to the pilot runbook and use it for canary gating
08:44 Priya Nair: any legal/procurement blockers we should know now? we might need standard DPAs and IP clauses
08:56 Samir Patel: procurement usually asks for DPA, security questionnaire - we'll send our standard DPA and the SCCs if required. Legal can loop in after pricing approval
09:12 Maya Ortiz: thanks, that works. one more question - if we need to rollback to an older architecture model, is there a compatibility matrix? e.g., some older models don't support function calling we use for structured outputs
09:30 Leah Wong: we have a model catalog with feature flags; we'll call out compatibility (function-calls, streaming, kv cache behavior) in the sheet. If a fallback lacks function-calls we can map to a reduced output flow or use a shim service to post-process
09:55 Connor Blake: ok good. also for observability we want traces mapped to our trace ids, can Redwood accept trace headers?
10:10 Samir Patel: yes trace header passthrough supported, and we can wire up per-request tracing for correlation
10:22 Priya Nair: recap and slate next steps?
10:28 Samir Patel: recap: pin A-v2 for checkout, B-quant fallback, Leah run benchmarks and share logs by Friday, Connor share traffic/profile and embedding sample by Friday, Samir send security deck and pricing spreadsheet by tomorrow. We'll schedule a short follow-up after benchmarks to finalize pinning for 2027-06-15 freeze.
10:50 Maya Ortiz: thanks all, that timeline works for us.
11:00 Meeting end
